profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a corporate law firm between the partner overseeing a client-facing thought leadership piece and the senior knowledge counsel supporting publication logistics. The firm is preparing a short client alert titled around 'The Boundaries of the Firm Revisited' for the firm's antitrust, M&A, and commercial contracts clients, using an academic discussion of transaction cost economics and property-rights theories as the conceptual anchor. The context is that the partner has already spoken informally with a major private equity client about circulating something 'early next week,' while the knowledge team is trying to fit the piece into the firm's standard publication workflow and archive taxonomy. The agenda is to align on who will produce which draft, what source package will accompany it, which version will go to marketing and conflicts, and what 'sign-off' and 'circulation' mean for each workstream. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on handoffs, timing, and shared documents so the piece can move from working draft to publication without further meetings.

members.name: Eleanor Price
members.expertise: M&A, joint ventures, and commercial contracting with a focus on governance and control rights
members.background: Eleanor is a senior partner who advises sponsors and strategic buyers on transaction structuring and frequently translates academic economic theories into practical boardroom guidance; she is used to lightweight internal coordination and fast-turn client alerts built from partner-marked drafts.
members.private_state: She wants to get a polished but fast client alert out before a competitor publishes on similar themes, and she is trying to avoid reopening substantive internal debate that could slow release.
hidden_assumptions: When she says 'the note,' she means the externally publishable client alert text, not the underlying research materials.
A 'clean draft' is a readable draft with her comments accepted and footnotes thinned, even if citation formatting and archive metadata are not yet finalized.
If she tells knowledge to 'send it to marketing,' that happens after partner-level substantive comfort and does not require full committee-style internal sign-off.
The 'core authorities' for this piece are the two foundational firm-boundary theories plus the few modern examples she marked up yesterday, rather than a full source-check package.
Circulating 'early next week' naturally means business-hours distribution to selected clients once the partner team is comfortable, even if internal repository steps happen later.

members.name: Daniel Cho
members.expertise: Knowledge management, publication governance, source validation, and cross-practice legal content coordination
members.background: Daniel is a former antitrust associate who now manages thought leadership workflows, publication standards, and legal content repositories; he regularly coordinates with marketing, conflicts, and library teams to turn attorney drafts into compliant firm publications.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the piece within the firm's publication protocol so it can be archived, repurposed, and defended if clients later rely on it, and he is concerned about informal publication outside the standard checks.
hidden_assumptions: When a partner refers to 'the note,' that usually includes the source list, abstract blurb, taxonomy tags, and publication-ready footnotes needed for the knowledge and marketing pipeline.
A 'clean draft' means scrubbed of unresolved comments, standardized citations, and ready for non-author teams to process without substantive guesswork.
Nothing is really 'sent to marketing' until the designated practice approver, knowledge review, and conflicts/publication checks are complete in the usual sequence.

The 'core authorities' for a theory-heavy piece should include all principal sources actually relied upon in the draft, including secondary literature and any case or policy materials used by implication.
A plan to circulate 'early next week' refers to the firm's regular client alert distribution list after repository intake and standard publication preparation are complete.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Eleanor will get Daniel a 'clean draft' by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Eleanor believes this means the article text after she accepts her own track changes and leaves only polished prose plus a few lean footnotes for later cleanup.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel believes this means a publication-ready document with resolved comments, complete citation formatting, and no ambiguities requiring knowledge-team judgment.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In law firm publication workflows, 'clean draft' is a routine phrase that feels self-explanatory; both use it constantly and neither expects the other to attach a materially different threshold to it.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss using 'the latest version' and 'yesterday's markup' as the basis for the next handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Eleanor is thinking of the Word document she revised after her evening call with a client, saved locally as a post-call draft with narrowed practical examples.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is thinking of the version in the firm's document management system that includes the library team's earlier inserted source placeholders and taxonomic header.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are referring to a perfectly plausible 'latest' file in a fast-moving workflow, and because each updated a different copy within hours of the other, the phrase does not feel like it needs disambiguation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Daniel will prepare the 'source package' once Eleanor sends over the draft.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Eleanor assumes the source package means the few foundational articles and perhaps one or two contemporary examples specifically cited in the client alert.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes the source package includes every authority needed to substantiate the piece end-to-end: foundational scholarship, any supporting cases or agency materials, secondary commentary, and the internal research notes necessary for archive completeness.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Source support is obviously needed, so the agreement sounds complete; the hidden divergence is about the invisible boundary of completeness, which usually only appears later when the receiving team starts assembling materials.

misalignment_points.topic: Meaning of 'signed off' and ready to circulate
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the note can be 'signed off' Monday and 'circulated' early next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Eleanor believes sign-off means she and one other relevant partner are substantively comfortable, after which the note can be shared with selected clients or sent to marketing for quick distribution.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel believes sign-off means completion of the firm's standard publication approvals, including knowledge review, practice approver confirmation, and the usual conflicts/publication checks required before broad circulation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are focused on moving the piece forward and use standard internal vocabulary associated with approval; because each assumes the firm's ordinary process naturally underlies the term, the difference in threshold remains invisible.
